review_result: Issues Found: 3 Major proof defects; 1 Minor normalization defect

problems.title: False uniform upper bound in Proposition 6.12
problems.proved_evidence: Exact conditional lower-row weights are 1/2 at endpoints and 1 internally, total L. Centered F equals (a0/ae)/L times [r^-1/2+sum_{v=1}^{L-1}r^{v-1}+r^{L-1}/2]. Its endpoint lower bound diverges with log sqrt(2)j-2log(j)+O(1), whereas the printed exponent including its actual absolute values is zero.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Actual absolute values were checked in image and retained; earlier extraction-based negative-exponent idea discarded.
The compact set is a legitimate singleton and epsilon follows actual application.
The weaker exp(C epsilon max|nu_i-M|) bound is proved in report and suffices with (6.36).
problems.core_dependency: (6.28) explicitly used on p.60 for limit under expectation in proof of Proposition6.14 -> Theorem1.3.
problems.repair_status: Sufficient replacement tail bound proved; dependent analytic inputs remain subject to P02.

independent_verification.assessment: Independently derived the k=2 free-fermion conditional row weights: endpoint weights 1/2, interior weights 1, total L. For t=0,gamma=pi/4,nu=(M,M+L),xi=(1,0), centered F is a0/(a_eps L)[r^-1/2+sum_(v=1)^(L-1)r^(v-1)+r^(L-1)/2]. The claimed exponent vanishes while n=2j^2,M=L=j^2,eps=n^-1/2 gives log lower bound sqrt(2)j-2log j+O(1). Rows are admissible and extendable. Actual source p60 uses (6.28) for core uniform integrability.
independent_verification.repair: Interlacing puts entries in [M-R,M+R]; |T_j-M-j| <=(2j-1)R+j and positive finite corner ratios yield C exp(C eps R). Source (6.36) at arbitrary positive exponential parameter suffices for this replacement tail step, conditional on preceding analytic inputs. This does not repair P02/P03.
independent_verification.counterevidence: No counterexample to the final GUE limit; printed absolute values and diffusive scaling do not save this bound.

problems.title: Antiferroelectric model has an n-dependent phase

hypotheses.domain: Fixed complex point off support, hence distance from real lattice exceeds epsilon/n for large n

problems.proved_evidence: Omega_n=(n+1)pi; saturated jump is +I for odd n, -I for even n. M22 even/odd ratio is theta4(v)theta3(0)/(theta3(v)theta4(0)); positive theta products give ratio>1 at v=pi/8. Nonidentical analytic functions also differ off real axis; persistent difference cannot be O(1/n).
problems.independent_computation: Theta series/product ratio1.0084627059602513; Abel quadrature at10+i gives |M22_even-M22_odd|0.0014108650655296903, non-interval illustration.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Not only hidden notation: footnote20 asserts independence.
Gamma rescaling does not remove phase and gamma=1 avoids rescaling.
Normalization at infinity supports possible unchanged GUE limit under uniformly controlled n-dependent prefactor.
problems.core_dependency: Proposition4.4 -> saddle prefactor and Lemma4.7 -> Theorem2.6 -> AF part of Theorem1.3.
problems.repair_status: Uniform n-dependent model/prefactor program specified; complete RHP uniformity proof not supplied.

independent_verification.assessment: At gamma=1,t=0 the cited model has Omega_n=(n+1)pi, hence alternating +I/-I saturated jump. Re-derived M22 even/odd ratio theta4(v)theta3(0)/(theta3(v)theta4(0). The positive convergent theta product is strictly larger than its v=0 value at v=pi/8. Ref (3.16), p16, gives u_infty/K=1/2; (8.7) and the increasing real Abel coordinate give 0<v<pi/4. Thus the report's fixed real point is available. Analytic continuation gives a fixed nonreal point satisfying lattice exclusion. O(1/n) cannot absorb persistent parity dependence. Source pp40-41 uses the fixed model in the saddle prefactor and fixed-function Lemma4.7.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Normalization at infinity and real-phase theta denominator positivity support an n-dependent uniformly bounded repair, but full contour/error estimates remain unverified. Does not disprove the limit.

problems.title: Ferroelectric origin Gamma factor is unbounded
source_locators: p.76 (A.34), invoked on p.89 immediately before (A.98); (A.95) is on p.89

hypotheses.approach: z ->0 along positive real axis inside origin disk

problems.proved_evidence: D_n(z)=Gamma(nz/2+3/2)e^(nz/2)/(sqrt(2pi)(nz/2)^(nz/2+1))~1/(sqrt(2)n z). The first column of S_n has nonzero finite limit because shifted monic orthogonal polynomial has all negative zeros. M(0) invertible; S_n D_n^sigma3 M^-1 has nonzero1/z leading coefficient. Uniform all-C X=I+O(1/n) fails.
problems.independent_computation: Gamma evaluations n10,100 and z1e-3,1e-5,1e-7 corroborate nzD limit and candidate recurrence.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: A.90 only away from origin is not contradicted.
Proposition4.6 conclusion is away from origin; only its printed global proof is invalidated.
D0=nz/(nz+1)D has finite one-sided limits, same imaginary-axis jump, valid large-z match.
problems.core_dependency: AppendixA.2 small-norm argument -> Proposition4.6 -> Theorem2.4 -> Theorem1.4.
problems.repair_status: Scalar candidate and recurrence proved; full matrix matching/jumps/small-norm repair unverified.
problems.acceptance_report_correction: Corrected report-only page locator for (A.95) from 88 to 89 and replaced incorrect attribution of the Cauchy representation to (A.100) with (A.34), invoked immediately before (A.98). Mathematical diagnosis and Major grade unchanged.

independent_verification.assessment: From the printed Gamma factor, D~1/(sqrt(2)n z) at fixed n. The shifted positive-weight orthogonal polynomial has only negative zeros; on the positive axis S's first column has a finite nonzero limit, while M(0) is invertible. Therefore S D^sigma3 M^-1 has a nonzero 1/z coefficient, contradicting global (A.98). Independently checked the Gamma recurrence for D0=nz/(nz+1)D, its two finite one-sided limits and cancellation at nz=-1.
independent_verification.counterevidence: (A.90) and Proposition4.6 are stated away from zero, so their conclusions are not directly disproved. Complete matrix matching/jump repair is not supplied by the scalar repair alone.
independent_verification.report_correction: (A.95) is on p89, not p88. The Cauchy representation is (A.34), p76, invoked before (A.98), not (A.100). Corrected current TeX and findings; original TeX/PDF/metadata preserved once.

problems.title: Ferroelectric base-measure normalization and infinite mass
problems.proved_evidence: Geometric sum of printed2sinh masses yields phi/2. n=1 absolute partition formula gives c/2 instead of c. Untilted atomic masses increase, so total mass infinite; formal phi(0)=-2coth(gamma) not a finite positive mass.
problems.independent_computation: Exact geometric formula, K200 finite sum with explicit discarded-tail bound; numerical ratio phi/Laplace2.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Exponential tilting at t0>gamma yields legitimate probability normalization.
Constant measure factors cancel from normalized laws and relevant polynomial ratios; no demonstrated core impact.
problems.core_dependency: No demonstrated dependency of the main normalized limit laws on this absolute normalization.
problems.repair_status: Local measure/formula correction given; no change of normalized laws from constant factor.

independent_verification.assessment: Summed the positive convergent geometric series for t>gamma>0: integral e^(tx)dm =1/(exp(2(t-gamma))-1)-1/(exp(2(t+gamma))-1)=phi/2. For n=1 the printed absolute partition identity gives c/2 instead of c. Untilted masses fail to tend to zero, hence total mass infinite; phi(0)=-2coth(gamma) is only analytic continuation outside the convergence domain.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Constant measure rescaling cancels from normalized log gas, monic OPs and measure/norm ratios, consistent with source footnote11. Thus peripheral Minor; exponential tilt t0>gamma supplies a genuine probability measure.
